22.description: A committee recommends City Council approve a $2.0 million budget increase for a Willows sanitary trunk pipe project on Melville Street, funded by reserves, to fix a deep pipe issue and enable neighborhood development.

chips.text: Staff explained a 9-meter deep pipe prevented pre-project investigation
Willows and Stonebridge neighborhoods will benefit from improved infrastructure.
Unused funds will be returned to reserves; costs recovered from development levies.

23.description: Saskatoon prioritized 22nd Street, 8th Street, and Woodlawn for future corridor development, guiding where 15% of the city's growth will be accommodated.

chips.text: Administration explained Preston's lower ranking due to equity, connectivity, and project alignment.
Equity was added as a new evaluation criterion for prioritizing plan areas this year.
Questions about the timeline and funding for physical construction in corridor plans remain.
Prioritization considered areas with higher social, economic, material, and housing needs.
The Nutana corridor plan is anticipated to be completed by the end of the year.

20.description: The committee recommends City Council refer the Marr Residence Management Board's updated Terms of Reference to administration for a report and receive its meeting procedures as information.

chips.text: Deputy City Clerk Bryant admitted an error in the initial recommendation.

24.description: Information regarding the Saskatoon Heritage Society's 50th Anniversary Celebrations was forwarded to the Municipal Heritage Advisory Committee for their review.

19.description: Saskatoon Council received the Municipal Heritage Advisory Committee's 2025 annual report, providing an update on heritage activities.

18.description: The Development Appeals Board reported a significant increase in appeals in 2025, mainly for setbacks and garage sizes. The fee for filing an appeal increased from $52 to $300.

chips.text: DAB Chair declined to state if bylaws are too restrictive, citing his role to interpret legislation.
Homeowners seeking larger detached garages are often appealing current bylaws.

21.description: Saskatoon City Council received the 2025 Annual Report from the Saskatoon North Partnership For Growth (P4G), providing an update on regional development.
